title: Generation of Scalable, Metallic High-Aspect Ratio Nanocomposites in a Biological Liquid Medium
protocol: Determine the volume of copper nanocomposites needed for synthesis.
Choose appropriate flasks based on the required volume.
Use a 37°C incubator with 5% CO2 and at least 40% humidity.
Prepare all materials fresh before starting an experiment.
Add solid materials to solvents immediately before beginning synthesis.
Keep stock solutions of cystine and copper dry after opening from the vendor by wrapping containers with Parafilm.
Weigh out at least 2 mg of copper nanoparticles.
Place the nanoparticles in an empty sterile 16 ml glass vial.
Add sterile deionized water to the vial containing CNPs to make a 2 mg/ml solution and vortex for 20 sec.
Sonicate the CNP solution for 17 min at room temperature.
Weigh out sufficient mass of cystine to make a 72.9 mg/ml solution for synthesis.
Place the weighed cystine in an antistatic weighing vessel.
Add sufficient volume of sterile, 1 M NaOH to the weighing vessel containing cystine so that the cystine completely dissolves.
Work in a sterile tissue culture hood.
Add 7 µl of cystine to 6,643 µl of sterile water in the sterile synthesis flask.
Incubate the mixture for 30 min at 37 °C with the flask cap vented.
Resuspend the 2 mg/ml CNP solution by vortexing for 30 sec.
Add 350 µl of resuspended CNPs to the cystine and water mixture using sterile technique.
Combine all components in a 25 cm² cell culture flask, maintaining the ratio of 1 part cystine, 50 parts CNPs, and 949 parts sterile water for a total synthesis volume of 7 ml as an example.
Replace the cap on the flask and tighten securely.
Gently mix the contents by swirling the flask 4-5 times.
Place the flask in the CO2 incubator and vent it by loosening the cap.
Incubate the mixture for approximately 24 hr with gas exchange.
Terminate synthesis of biocomposites by tightly capping the synthesis flask and storing the vessel in a refrigerator (4 °C).
Label the flask with synthesis conditions, including components utilized, date of the synthesis, and incubation time of the synthesis before termination.
Dissolve at least 2 mg of copper sulfate in sufficient volume of sterile deionized water to make a 2 mg/ml solution.
Vortex the vial if needed to ensure all crystals are dissolved.
Inspect by eye to confirm all crystals have dissolved.
Carry out self-assembly synthesis using the prepared copper sulfate solution as described previously, replacing CNPs with copper sulfate.
Terminate the synthesis of copper sulfate biocomposites as described for CNP composites (step 2.6).
Store copper sulfate biocomposites long-term at 4 °C.
Characterize biocomposites derived from CNPs and copper sulfate by white light microscopy.
Use an inverted microscope to characterize post-synthesis biocomposites, as they settle to the bottom of the flask within a few minutes when laid flat.
Employ the bright field setting on the microscope to enhance contrast between biocomposites and liquid medium.
Capture images of composites using a digital camera connected to the microscope.
Allow flasks containing biocomposites to come to room temperature for at least 15 minutes after removal from the refrigerator.
Wipe the top and bottom surfaces of the flask with a clean paper towel to maximize microscopy imaging quality.
Vortex the flask for 30 seconds to dissociate clumps of composites that form while in storage.
Inspect the structures with an inverted microscope to ensure aggregates have dissociated, repeating vortexing as necessary.
Use inverted white light microscopy to assess the efficacy of the synthesis for a given experiment using CNPs.
Avoid carrying out synthesis for too long before termination to prevent highly branched “urchin” type structures.
Use inverted white light microscopy to assess the efficacy of the synthesis using copper sulfate.
Compare flasks with different synthesis conditions such as time of synthesis before termination.
Centrifuge solutions of biocomposites in a centrifuge tube.
Add 6 ml of either CNP-derived structures or copper sulfate-derived structures to a 15 ml centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 500 x g at room temperature to form a pellet.
For smaller volumes, add 500 μl of structures in solution to 0.6 ml sized tubes.
Centrifuge at 2,000 x g at room temperature for at least 10 min to form a pellet.
Save the observable pellet at the bottom of the tube after centrifuging for sufficient time (at least 10 min).
Carefully remove the supernatant liquid above the pellet to concentrate structures.
Add more composites to this tube and repeat the process in the same tube if desired.
Disperse concentrated pellets by adding the desired volume of solution to the tube.
Vortex for 10-30 seconds to disperse the concentrated pellets.
Sonicate structures once formed, to move the average population size (lengths) of the structures to lower values.
Place structures in sterile deionized water and sonicate for at least 10 min.
Document changes in composite sizes with different sonication times using an inverted white light microscope and digital camera.
